answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller, whether named zephyr, juniper, or reef, to lock a separate $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs. A contract slashes the bond if anyone submits two receipts signed by that seller claiming different results for the same job. Creating 1,000 eligible identities therefore ties up $100,000: names are cheap, but each usable account consumes capital and risks losing its bond for provable equivocation.
